disallow_untyped_defs = True

[pydantic-mypy]
init_forbid_extra = True
init_typed = True
warn_required_dynamic_aliases = True
```

--------------------------------

### Wrap model serializer with @model_serializer

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/serialization.md

A wrap model serializer requires a handler parameter that delegates to Pydantic's serialization. You can run code before or after calling the handler, or skip it entirely.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, SerializerFunctionWrapHandler, model_serializer


class UserModel(BaseModel):
    username: str
    password: str

    @model_serializer(mode='wrap')
    def serialize_model(
        self, handler: SerializerFunctionWrapHandler
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        serialized = handler(self)
        serialized['fields'] = list(serialized)
        return serialized


print(UserModel(username='foo', password='bar').model_dump())
#> {'username': 'foo', 'password': 'bar', 'fields': ['username', 'password']}
```

--------------------------------

### Customize $ref references using ref_template

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/json_schema.md

Specify a custom prefix format for `$ref` definitions using the `ref_template` parameter in `json_schema()` or `model_json_schema()`. Definitions remain stored under `$defs` while referencing the custom schema path format.

```python
import json

from pydantic import BaseModel
from pydantic.type_adapter import TypeAdapter


class Foo(BaseModel):
    a: int


class Model(BaseModel):
    a: Foo


adapter = TypeAdapter(Model)

print(
    json.dumps(
        adapter.json_schema(ref_template='#/components/schemas/{model}'),
        indent=2,
    )
)
"""
{
  "$defs": {
    "Foo": {
      "properties": {
        "a": {
          "title": "A",
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "a"
      ],
      "title": "Foo",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "properties": {
    "a": {
      "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Foo"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "a"
  ],
  "title": "Model",
  "type": "object"
}
"""
```

### Customize Field JSON Schema Attributes

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/json_schema.md

Customizes field schema metadata such as description, title, examples, and additional properties via json_schema_extra using Field() and Annotated.

```python
import json
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import BaseModel, EmailStr, Field, SecretStr


class User(BaseModel):
    age: int = Field(description='Age of the user')
    email: Annotated[EmailStr, Field(examples=['marcelo@mail.com'])]  # (1)!
    name: str = Field(title='Username')
    password: SecretStr = Field(
        json_schema_extra={
            'title': 'Password',
            'description': 'Password of the user',
            'examples': ['123456'],
        }
    )


print(json.dumps(User.model_json_schema(), indent=2))
"""
{
  "properties": {
    "age": {
      "description": "Age of the user",
      "title": "Age",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "email": {
      "examples": [
        "marcelo@mail.com"
      ],
      "format": "email",
      "title": "Email",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "name": {
      "title": "Username",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "password": {
      "description": "Password of the user",
      "examples": [
        "123456"
      ],
      "format": "password",
      "title": "Password",
      "type": "string",
      "writeOnly": true
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "age",
    "email",
    "name",
    "password"
  ],
  "title": "User",
  "type": "object"
}
"""
```

### Extend a base model with create_model using __base__

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/models.md

Use the __base__ keyword to extend an existing model with additional fields. The printed output shows the resulting class and its model_fields keys.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, create_model


class FooModel(BaseModel):
    foo: str
    bar: int = 123


BarModel = create_model(
    'BarModel',
    apple=(str, 'russet'),
    banana=(str, 'yellow'),
    __base__=FooModel,
)
print(BarModel)
#> <class '__main__.BarModel'>
print(BarModel.model_fields.keys())
#> dict_keys(['foo', 'bar', 'apple', 'banana'])
```

### Access serialization context in a field_serializer

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/serialization.md

Pass a context dict to model_dump and read it via info.context inside a field_serializer to customize output. Without a context, the value is returned unchanged.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, FieldSerializationInfo, field_serializer


class Model(BaseModel):
    text: str

    @field_serializer('text', mode='plain')
    @classmethod
    def remove_stopwords(cls, v: str, info: FieldSerializationInfo) -> str:
        if isinstance(info.context, dict):
            stopwords = info.context.get('stopwords', set())
            v = ' '.join(w for w in v.split() if w.lower() not in stopwords)
        return v


model = Model(text='This is an example document')
print(model.model_dump())  # no context
#> {'text': 'This is an example document'}
print(model.model_dump(context={'stopwords': ['this', 'is', 'an']}))
#> {'text': 'example document'}
```

### Field Serializer with Serialization Info

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/serialization.md

A field serializer can optionally accept an `info` argument of type `FieldSerializationInfo`, which provides access to the serialization context, mode, and other parameters. This example shows a field serializer that uses the context to remove stopwords from a string field.

```APIDOC
## Field Serializer with Serialization Info

### Description
A field serializer can optionally accept an `info` argument of type `FieldSerializationInfo`, which provides access to the serialization context, mode, and other parameters. This example shows a field serializer that uses the context to remove stopwords from a string field.

### Method
`@field_serializer` decorator

### Parameters
#### Serializer Function Parameters
- **v** (str) - Required - The field value to serialize.
- **info** (FieldSerializationInfo) - Optional - Provides extra information such as `context`, `mode`, and `field_name`.

### Request Example
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, FieldSerializationInfo, field_serializer

class Model(BaseModel):
    text: str

    @field_serializer('text', mode='plain')
    @classmethod
    def remove_stopwords(cls, v: str, info: FieldSerializationInfo) -> str:
        if isinstance(info.context, dict):
            stopwords = info.context.get('stopwords', set())
            v = ' '.join(w for w in v.split() if w.lower() not in stopwords)
        return v

model = Model(text='This is an example document')
print(model.model_dump())  # no context
#> {'text': 'This is an example document'}
print(model.model_dump(context={'stopwords': ['this', 'is', 'an']}))
#> {'text': 'example document'}
```

### Response
#### Success Response
- **dict** - The serialized model data.

#### Response Example
```python
{'text': 'example document'}
```
```

### Merge Subclass and Parent Model Configuration

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/config.md

Provide a new `model_config` in a subclass to merge with and override parent settings. Note that Pydantic does not currently follow MRO when inheriting from multiple bases.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Parent(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow', str_to_lower=False)


class Model(Parent):
    model_config = ConfigDict(str_to_lower=True)

    x: str


m = Model(x='FOO', y='bar')
print(m.model_dump())
#> {'x': 'foo', 'y': 'bar'}
print(Model.model_config)
#> {'extra': 'allow', 'str_to_lower': True}
```

### Generate model title programmatically using model_title_generator

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/json_schema.md

Applies a title generator function to the model itself via ConfigDict. The generator function receives the model class as input.

```python
import json

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


def make_title(model: type) -> str:
    return f'Title-{model.__name__}'


class Person(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(model_title_generator=make_title)
    name: str
    age: int


print(json.dumps(Person.model_json_schema(), indent=2))
"""
{
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "title": "Name",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "age": {
      "title": "Age",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name",
    "age"
  ],
  "title": "Title-Person",
  "type": "object"
}
"""
```

### Allow extra data with ConfigDict(extra='allow')

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/models.md

Set extra='allow' to store extra data in the __pydantic_extra__ dictionary attribute. If extra were set to 'forbid', providing extra data would fail.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Model(BaseModel):
    x: int

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow')


m = Model(x=1, y='a')  # (1)!
assert m.model_dump() == {'x': 1, 'y': 'a'}
assert m.__pydantic_extra__ == {'y': 'a'}
```

### Define private model attributes with PrivateAttr

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/models.md

Attributes with a leading underscore are converted into private attributes that are not validated or set during __init__ or model_validate. Use PrivateAttr with default_factory or set values in model_post_init; dunder names are not supported.

```python
from datetime import datetime
from random import randint
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, PrivateAttr


class TimeAwareModel(BaseModel):
    _processed_at: datetime = PrivateAttr(default_factory=datetime.now)
    _secret_value: str

    def model_post_init(self, context: Any) -> None:
        # this could also be done with `default_factory`:
        self._secret_value = randint(1, 5)


m = TimeAwareModel()
print(m._processed_at)
#> 2032-01-02 03:04:05.000006
print(m._secret_value)
#> 3
```

### Validate set and frozenset fields with Pydantic BaseModel

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/api/standard_library_types.md

Defines a model with a `set` and a `frozenset[int]` field. Input lists are converted to a set and a frozenset, with items validated against the parameter type.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel


class Model(BaseModel):
    simple_set: set | None = None
    set_of_ints: frozenset[int] | None = None


print(Model(simple_set=['1', '2', '3']).simple_set)
#> {'1', '2', '3'}
print(Model(set_of_ints=['1', '2', '3']).set_of_ints)
#> frozenset({1, 2, 3})
```

### Configure strict mode on a model and override at field level

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

### Configure validate_call with ConfigDict

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/validation_decorator.md

Use the config parameter on @validate_call to specify custom settings such as arbitrary_types_allowed. Raises a ValidationError when invalid argument types are supplied.

```python
from pydantic import ConfigDict, ValidationError, validate_call


class Foobar:
    def __init__(self, v: str):
        self.v = v

    def __add__(self, other: 'Foobar') -> str:
        return f'{self} + {other}'

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f'Foobar({self.v})'


@validate_call(config=ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True))
def add_foobars(a: Foobar, b: Foobar):
    return a + b


c = add_foobars(Foobar('a'), Foobar('b'))
print(c)
#> Foobar(a) + Foobar(b)

try:
    add_foobars(1, 2)
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)
    """
    2 validation errors for add_foobars
    0
      Input should be an instance of Foobar [type=is_instance_of, input_value=1, input_type=int]
    1
      Input should be an instance of Foobar [type=is_instance_of, input_value=2, input_type=int]
    """
```

### Configure JsonSchemaMode for validation and serialization

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/json_schema.md

Pass the mode parameter to model_json_schema to generate schemas tailored either for validation or serialization behavior. By default, mode is set to 'validation'.

```python
from decimal import Decimal

from pydantic import BaseModel


class Model(BaseModel):
    a: Decimal = Decimal('12.34')


print(Model.model_json_schema(mode='validation'))
"""
{
    'properties': {
        'a': {
            'anyOf': [{'type': 'number'}, {'type': 'string'}],
            'default': '12.34',
            'title': 'A',
        }
    },
    'title': 'Model',
    'type': 'object',
}
"""

print(Model.model_json_schema(mode='serialization'))
"""
{
    'properties': {'a': {'default': '12.34', 'title': 'A', 'type': 'string'}}},
    'title': 'Model',
    'type': 'object',
}
"""
```

### Configuring TypeAdapter with ConfigDict

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/config.md

Pass ConfigDict to the TypeAdapter config argument to apply custom validation settings such as coercing numbers to strings. A usage error is raised if the wrapped type directly supports configuration.

```python
from pydantic import ConfigDict, TypeAdapter

ta = TypeAdapter(list[str], config=ConfigDict(coerce_numbers_to_str=True))

print(ta.validate_python([1, 2]))
#> ['1', '2']
```

### Configure frozen model with ConfigDict(frozen=True)

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/models.md

Set model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True) to make instance attributes immutable; assigning to a field raises a ValidationError with type=frozen_instance. Nested mutable values like dicts can still be modified, since immutability is not enforced in Python.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, ValidationError


class FooBarModel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    a: str
    b: dict


foobar = FooBarModel(a='hello', b={'apple': 'pear'})

try:
    foobar.a = 'different'
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)
    """
    1 validation error for FooBarModel
    a
      Instance is frozen [type=frozen_instance, input_value='different', input_type=str]
    """

print(foobar.a)
#> hello
print(foobar.b)
#> {'apple': 'pear'}
foobar.b['apple'] = 'grape'
print(foobar.b)
#> {'apple': 'grape'}

```

--------------------------------

### Exclude unset fields with exclude_unset

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/serialization.md

Use `exclude_unset=True` to exclude fields not explicitly set during instantiation. Altering a field after creation removes it from the unset fields.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel


class UserModel(BaseModel):
    name: str
    age: int = 18


user = UserModel(name='John')
print(user.model_fields_set)
#> {'name'}

print(user.model_dump(exclude_unset=True))
#> {'name': 'John'}
```

```python
user.age = 21

print(user.model_dump(exclude_unset=True))
#> {'name': 'John', 'age': 21}
```

--------------------------------

### Merge Subclass and Parent Model Configuration

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/config.md

Provide a new `model_config` in a subclass to merge with and override parent settings. Note that Pydantic does not currently follow MRO when inheriting from multiple bases.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Parent(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow', str_to_lower=False)


class Model(Parent):
    model_config = ConfigDict(str_to_lower=True)

    x: str


m = Model(x='FOO', y='bar')
print(m.model_dump())
#> {'x': 'foo', 'y': 'bar'}
print(Model.model_config)
#> {'extra': 'allow', 'str_to_lower': True}
```

--------------------------------

### Triggering root-model-extra error when configuring extra fields on RootModel

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/errors/usage_errors.md

Raised when setting model_config['extra'] on a RootModel subclass, because RootModel cannot accept or store extra fields during initialization.

```python
from pydantic import PydanticUserError, RootModel

try:

    class MyRootModel(RootModel):
        model_config = {'extra': 'allow'}
        root: int

except PydanticUserError as exc_info:
    assert exc_info.code == 'root-model-extra'
```

--------------------------------

### Raise set_item_not_hashable for unhashable set values

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/errors/validation_errors.md

Validating an unhashable value against a set or frozenset field raises set_item_not_hashable. Both the dict and the Unhashable instance produce this error type.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError


class Model(BaseModel):
    x: set[object]


class Unhashable:
    __hash__ = None


try:
    Model(x=[{'a': 'b'}, Unhashable()])
except ValidationError as exc:
    print(repr(exc.errors()[0]['type']))
    #> 'set_item_not_hashable'
    print(repr(exc.errors()[1]['type']))
    #> 'set_item_not_hashable'
```

### Use serialize_as_any runtime setting in model_dump()

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/serialization.md

Pass serialize_as_any=True to model_dump() to include subclass fields; with False (the V2 default), fields present only on the subclass are excluded from serialization.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel


class User(BaseModel):
    name: str


class UserLogin(User):
    password: str


class OuterModel(BaseModel):
    user1: User
    user2: User


user = UserLogin(name='pydantic', password='password')

outer_model = OuterModel(user1=user, user2=user)
print(outer_model.model_dump(serialize_as_any=True))  # (1)!
"""
{
    'user1': {'name': 'pydantic', 'password': 'password'},
    'user2': {'name': 'pydantic', 'password': 'password'},
}
"""

print(outer_model.model_dump(serialize_as_any=False))  # (2)!
#> {'user1': {'name': 'pydantic'}, 'user2': {'name': 'pydantic'}}

```

--------------------------------

### Triggering 'validate-by-alias-and-name-false' in ConfigDict

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/errors/usage_errors.md

Raises PydanticUserError with code 'validate-by-alias-and-name-false' when both validate_by_alias and validate_by_name are set to False.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, PydanticUserError

try:

    class Model(BaseModel):
        a: int = Field(alias='A')

        model_config = ConfigDict(
            validate_by_alias=False, validate_by_name=False
        )

except PydanticUserError as exc_info:
    assert exc_info.code == 'validate-by-alias-and-name-false'
```

--------------------------------

### Allow arbitrary types in standard library dataclasses with arbitrary_types_allowed

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/dataclasses.md

Set `arbitrary_types_allowed=True` in `ConfigDict` on a parent model to allow custom arbitrary types in nested standard library dataclasses without raising `PydanticSchemaGenerationError`.

```python
import dataclasses

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
from pydantic.errors import PydanticSchemaGenerationError


class ArbitraryType:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'ArbitraryType(value={self.value!r})'


@dataclasses.dataclass
class DC:
    a: ArbitraryType
    b: str


# valid as it is a stdlib dataclass without validation:
my_dc = DC(a=ArbitraryType(value=3), b='qwe')

try:

    class Model(BaseModel):
        dc: DC
        other: str

    # invalid as dc is now validated with pydantic, and ArbitraryType is not a known type
    Model(dc=my_dc, other='other')

except PydanticSchemaGenerationError as e:
    print(e.message)
    """
    Unable to generate pydantic-core schema for <class '__main__.ArbitraryType'>. Set `arbitrary_types_allowed=True` in the model_config to ignore this error or implement `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` on your type to fully support it.

    If you got this error by calling handler(<some type>) within `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` then you likely need to call `handler.generate_schema(<some type>)` since we do not call `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` on `<some type>` otherwise to avoid infinite recursion.
    """


# valid as we set arbitrary_types_allowed=True, and that config pushes down to the nested vanilla dataclass
class Model(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)

    dc: DC
    other: str


m = Model(dc=my_dc, other='other')
print(repr(m))
#> Model(dc=DC(a=ArbitraryType(value=3), b='qwe'), other='other')
```

### Access model fields and verify coercion

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/models.md

Accesses fields as attributes. The default name is used since it wasn't set, and the string '123' is coerced to integer 123.

```python
assert user.name == 'Jane Doe'  # (1)!
assert user.id == 123  # (2)!
assert isinstance(user.id, int)
```

Demonstrates setting validation_alias on a model field, which type checkers do not natively recognize.

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class MyModel(BaseModel):

### Enabling strict mode on fields with Field(strict=True)

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/strict_mode.md

Set `strict=True` on individual fields using `Field()` to enforce strict type checking regardless of whether validation is called in lax mode. Passing values with mismatched types raises a `ValidationError`.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError


class User(BaseModel):
    name: str
    age: int = Field(strict=True)  # (1)!


user = User(name='John', age=42)
print(user)
#> name='John' age=42


try:
    another_user = User(name='John', age='42')
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)
    """
    1 validation error for User
    age
      Input should be a valid integer [type=int_type, input_value='42', input_type=str]
    """
```

### Resolving Missing Annotations with ConfigDict ignored_types

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/errors/usage_errors.md

Exempts specific types from being treated as model fields by setting ignored_types in model_config.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class IgnoredType:
    pass


class MyModel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(ignored_types=(IgnoredType,))

    _a = IgnoredType()
    _b: int = IgnoredType()
    _c: IgnoredType
    _d: IgnoredType = IgnoredType()
```

--------------------------------

### Exclude and include specific fields with model_dump()

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/serialization.md

Use `exclude` with a set or dictionary to exclude fields, or `include` to include only specified fields. Using `False` to include a field in `exclude` (or exclude a field in `include`) is not supported.

```python
# using a set:
print(t.model_dump(exclude={'user', 'value'}))
#> {'id': '1234567890'}

# using a dictionary:
print(t.model_dump(exclude={'user': {'username', 'password'}, 'value': True}))
#> {'id': '1234567890', 'user': {'id': 42}}

# same configuration using `include`:
print(t.model_dump(include={'id': True, 'user': {'id'}}))
#> {'id': '1234567890', 'user': {'id': 42}}
```

### Validate using both by_alias and by_name

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/alias.md

Set both `by_alias=True` and `by_name=True` to allow validation by either alias or attribute name. Both `my_alias` and `my_field` are accepted.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Model(BaseModel):
    my_field: str = Field(validation_alias='my_alias')


m = Model.model_validate(
    {'my_alias': 'foo'}, by_alias=True, by_name=True  # (1)!
)
print(repr(m))
#> Model(my_field='foo')

m = Model.model_validate(
    {'my_field': 'foo'}, by_alias=True, by_name=True  # (2)!
)
print(repr(m))
#> Model(my_field='foo')
```

### Perform Partial Validation with TypeAdapter

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/experimental.md

Demonstrates validating incomplete JSON strings and Python objects using TypeAdapter.validate_json and TypeAdapter.validate_python with experimental_allow_partial set to True or 'trailing-strings'.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from annotated_types import MinLen
from typing_extensions import NotRequired, TypedDict

from pydantic import TypeAdapter


class Foobar(TypedDict):  # (1)!
    a: int
    b: NotRequired[float]
    c: NotRequired[Annotated[str, MinLen(5)]]


ta = TypeAdapter(list[Foobar])

v = ta.validate_json('[{"a": 1, "b"', experimental_allow_partial=True)  # (2)!
print(v)
#> [{'a': 1}]

v = ta.validate_json(
    '[{"a": 1, "b": 1.0, "c": "abcd', experimental_allow_partial=True  # (3)!
)
print(v)
#> [{'a': 1, 'b': 1.0}]

v = ta.validate_json(
    '[{"b": 1.0, "c": "abcde"', experimental_allow_partial=True  # (4)!
)
print(v)
#> []

v = ta.validate_json(
    '[{"a": 1, "b": 1.0, "c": "abcde"},{"a": ', experimental_allow_partial=True
)
print(v)
#> [{'a': 1, 'b': 1.0, 'c': 'abcde'}]

v = ta.validate_python([{'a': 1}], experimental_allow_partial=True)  # (5)!
print(v)
#> [{'a': 1}]

v = ta.validate_python(
    [{'a': 1, 'b': 1.0, 'c': 'abcd'}], experimental_allow_partial=True  # (6)!
)
print(v)
#> [{'a': 1, 'b': 1.0}]

v = ta.validate_json(
    '[{"a": 1, "b": 1.0, "c": "abcdefg',
    experimental_allow_partial='trailing-strings',  # (7)!
)
print(v)
#> [{'a': 1, 'b': 1.0, 'c': 'abcdefg'}]
```

### Describe function parameters with Field and validate_call

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/validation_decorator.md

Use Annotated with Field for required parameters or set Field as a default value to provide metadata and validation constraints on decorated function arguments.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import Field, ValidationError, validate_call


@validate_call
def how_many(num: Annotated[int, Field(gt=10)]):
    return num


try:
    how_many(1)
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)
    """
    1 validation error for how_many
    0
      Input should be greater than 10 [type=greater_than, input_value=1, input_type=int]
    """


@validate_call
def return_value(value: str = Field(default='default value')):
    return value


print(return_value())
#> default value
```

### Pass Options to Pydantic Plugins via plugin_settings

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/config.md

Pass configuration options to plugins like Logfire using `plugin_settings` during model class definition. The configuration takes a dictionary keyed by plugin name.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel


class User(BaseModel, plugin_settings={'logfire': {'record': 'failure'}}):
    name: str
    email: str
```

### Validate union fields using left_to_right mode

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/unions.md

Sets `union_mode='left_to_right'` on a `Field` to attempt validation on union types in their defined order. If validation fails across all members, the resulting `ValidationError` aggregates errors from each member.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError


class User(BaseModel):
    id: str | int = Field(union_mode='left_to_right')


print(User(id=123))
#> id=123
print(User(id='hello'))
#> id='hello'

try:
    User(id=[])
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)
    """
    2 validation errors for User
    id.str
      Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=[], input_type=list]
    id.int
      Input should be a valid integer [type=int_type, input_value=[], input_type=list]
    """
```

### Bypassing field validation checks with check_fields=False

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/errors/usage_errors.md

Set check_fields=False on @field_validator when the validated field will be defined on an inherited or dynamically generated model.

```python
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, create_model, field_validator


class Model(BaseModel):
    @field_validator('a', check_fields=False)
    def check_a(cls, v: Any):
        return v


model = create_model('FooModel', a=(str, 'cake'), __base__=Model)
```

--------------------------------

### Specifying json_schema_input_type on field_validator

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/validators.md

Sets the json_schema_input_type argument on @field_validator to explicitly define accepted input types in the generated JSON Schema.

```python
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator


class Model(BaseModel):
    value: str

    @field_validator('value', mode='before', json_schema_input_type=int | str)
    @classmethod
    def cast_ints(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
        if isinstance(value, int):
            return str(value)
        else:
            return value


print(Model.model_json_schema()['properties']['value'])
#> {'anyOf': [{'type': 'integer'}, {'type': 'string'}], 'title': 'Value'}
```

Shows that Pydantic performs data conversion by default, so passing a string to an int field is valid at runtime. This motivates the init_typed setting.

```python
class Model(BaseModel):
    a: int


Model(a='1')

### Prevent field reassignment using Field(frozen=True)

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/fields.md

Sets `frozen=True` to enforce field immutability after model creation. Attempting to assign a new value to a frozen field raises a `ValidationError`.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError


class User(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(frozen=True)
    age: int


user = User(name='John', age=42)

try:
    user.name = 'Jane'  # (1)!
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)
    """
    1 validation error for User
    name
      Field is frozen [type=frozen_field, input_value='Jane', input_type=str]
    """
```

### Define discriminated unions with string discriminators

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/unions.md

Set a common Literal field on each union model and pass the discriminator field name to Field(discriminator=...). Validation targets only the matched model, preventing error proliferation across all union members.

```python
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError


class Cat(BaseModel):
    pet_type: Literal['cat']
    meows: int


class Dog(BaseModel):
    pet_type: Literal['dog']
    barks: float


class Lizard(BaseModel):
    pet_type: Literal['reptile', 'lizard']
    scales: bool


class Model(BaseModel):
    pet: Cat | Dog | Lizard = Field(discriminator='pet_type')
    n: int


print(Model(pet={'pet_type': 'dog', 'barks': 3.14}, n=1))
#> pet=Dog(pet_type='dog', barks=3.14) n=1
try:
    Model(pet={'pet_type': 'dog'}, n=1)
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)
    """
    1 validation error for Model
    pet.dog.barks
      Field required [type=missing, input_value={'pet_type': 'dog'}, input_type=dict]
    """
```

### Serialize subclass fields with polymorphic_serialization runtime setting

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/serialization.md

Defines a base model `User` and subclass `UserLogin`, then serializes an `OuterModel` containing a `UserLogin` instance. Without the runtime flag, only base fields are dumped; with `polymorphic_serialization=True`, subclass fields such as `password` are included.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel


class User(BaseModel):  # (1)!
    name: str


class UserLogin(User):
    password: str


class OuterModel(BaseModel):
    user: User


outer_model = OuterModel(
    user=UserLogin(name='pydantic', password='password'),
)


print(outer_model.model_dump())  # (2)!
#> {'user': {'name': 'pydantic'}}
print(outer_model.model_dump(polymorphic_serialization=True))  # (3)!
#> {'user': {'name': 'pydantic', 'password': 'password'}}
```

### Configure Pydantic models using model_config

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/config.md

Defines configuration options on a Pydantic model using the ConfigDict class assigned to model_config. A plain dictionary can also be used instead of ConfigDict.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, ValidationError


class Model(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(str_max_length=5)  # (1)!

    v: str


try:
    m = Model(v='abcdef')
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)
    """
    1 validation error for Model
    v
      String should have at most 5 characters [type=string_too_long, input_value='abcdef', input_type=str]
    """
```

### Configure Pydantic dataclass using config parameter or __pydantic_config__

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/dataclasses.md

Configure dataclass behavior by passing a ConfigDict to the @dataclass decorator config parameter or by defining the __pydantic_config__ class attribute.

from pydantic import ConfigDict

### Enforce validation on default values using validate_default

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/fields.md

Enables validation on field default values. By default Pydantic does not validate defaults; setting validate_default=True causes invalid defaults to raise a ValidationError upon instantiation.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError


class User(BaseModel):
    age: int = Field(default='twelve', validate_default=True)


try:
    user = User()
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)
    """
    1 validation error for User
    age
      Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer [type=int_parsing, input_value='twelve', input_type=str]
    """
```

### Validate using both alias and name with validate_by_alias and validate_by_name

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/alias.md

Set both validate_by_alias=True and validate_by_name=True to accept either the alias 'my_alias' or the attribute name 'my_field'. When both are provided, the alias takes precedence.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


class Model(BaseModel):
    my_field: str = Field(validation_alias='my_alias')

    model_config = ConfigDict(validate_by_alias=True, validate_by_name=True)


print(repr(Model(my_alias='foo')))  # (1)!
#> Model(my_field='foo')

print(repr(Model(my_field='foo')))  # (2)!
#> Model(my_field='foo')

print(repr(Model(my_alias='foo', my_field='bar')))  # (3)!
#> Model(my_field='foo')
```

### Raise frozen_instance error with ConfigDict(frozen=True)

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/errors/validation_errors.md

When `frozen=True` is set in `model_config`, assigning to or deleting any field raises a `ValidationError` whose first error type is `'frozen_instance'`.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, ValidationError


class Model(BaseModel):
    x: int

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)


m = Model(x=1)

try:
    m.x = 2
except ValidationError as exc:
    print(repr(exc.errors()[0]['type']))
    #> 'frozen_instance'

try:
    del m.x
except ValidationError as exc:
    print(repr(exc.errors()[0]['type']))
    #> 'frozen_instance'
```

### Configure dataclass fields with Field parameters

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/fields.md

Apply Field() parameters such as init_var and kw_only to Pydantic dataclasses. Init-only fields (init_var=True) are passed to initialization but excluded from serialized output like model_dump().

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from pydantic.dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class Foo:
    bar: str
    baz: str = Field(init_var=True)
    qux: str = Field(kw_only=True)


class Model(BaseModel):
    foo: Foo


model = Model(foo=Foo('bar', baz='baz', qux='qux'))
print(model.model_dump())  # (1)!
#> {'foo': {'bar': 'bar', 'qux': 'qux'}}
```

### Validate SQLAlchemy ORM object with from_attributes

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/models.md

Uses model_validate with from_attributes=True to validate an SQLAlchemy ORM instance. The model_config sets from_attributes to enable attribute-based validation.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from sqlalchemy import ARRAY, String
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, StringConstraints


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class CompanyOrm(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'companies'

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True, nullable=False)
    public_key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(20), index=True, nullable=False, unique=True
    )
    domains: Mapped[list[str]] = mapped_column(ARRAY(String(255)))


class CompanyModel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    id: int
    public_key: Annotated[str, StringConstraints(max_length=20)]
    domains: list[Annotated[str, StringConstraints(max_length=255)]]


co_orm = CompanyOrm(
    id=123,
    public_key='foobar',
    domains=['example.com', 'foobar.com'],
)
print(co_orm)
#> <__main__.CompanyOrm object at 0x0123456789ab>
co_model = CompanyModel.model_validate(co_orm)
print(co_model)
#> id=123 public_key='foobar' domains=['example.com', 'foobar.com']
```

### Configure fields using dataclasses.field and Pydantic Field

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/dataclasses.md

Pydantic dataclasses support both standard library dataclasses.field and Pydantic's Field for metadata, default values, and constraint validation.

```python
import dataclasses

from pydantic import Field
from pydantic.dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class User:
    id: int
    name: str = 'John Doe'
    friends: list[int] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=lambda: [0])
    age: int | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None,
        metadata={'title': 'The age of the user', 'description': 'do not lie!'},
    )
    height: int | None = Field(
        default=None, title='The height in cm', ge=50, le=300
    )


user = User(id='42', height='250')
print(user)
#> User(id=42, name='John Doe', friends=[0], age=None, height=250)
```

### Triggering 'config-both' Error

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/errors/usage_errors.md

Raised when both class Config and model_config are defined within the same model.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, PydanticUserError

try:

    class Model(BaseModel):
        model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

        a: str

        class Config:
            from_attributes = True

except PydanticUserError as exc_info:
    assert exc_info.code == 'config-both'
```

### Propagating configuration to standard library dataclasses with with_config override

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/config.md

Configuration propagates down to standard library dataclasses and typed dictionaries unless the type defines its own configuration. Here, user_1 inherits str_to_lower=True while user_2 overrides it with @with_config(str_to_lower=False).

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, with_config


@dataclass
class UserWithoutConfig:
    name: str


@dataclass
@with_config(str_to_lower=False)
class UserWithConfig:
    name: str


class Parent(BaseModel):
    user_1: UserWithoutConfig
    user_2: UserWithConfig

    model_config = ConfigDict(str_to_lower=True)


print(Parent(user_1={'name': 'JOHN'}, user_2={'name': 'JOHN'}))
#> user_1=UserWithoutConfig(name='john') user_2=UserWithConfig(name='JOHN')
```

### Derive a model with all fields made optional using create_model()

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/examples/dynamic_models.md

Dynamically creates a new model from an existing BaseModel subclass with all fields made optional with a default of None. Setting __base__ inherits validators and computed fields from the parent model.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, create_model


def make_fields_optional(model_cls: type[BaseModel]) -> type[BaseModel]:
    new_fields = {}

    for f_name, f_info in model_cls.model_fields.items():
        f_dct = f_info.asdict()
        new_fields[f_name] = (
            Annotated[(f_dct['annotation'] | None, *f_dct['metadata'], Field(**f_dct['attributes']))],
            None,
        )

    return create_model(
        f'{model_cls.__name__}Optional',
        __base__=model_cls,  # (1)!
        **new_fields,
    )
```

```python
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, create_model


def make_fields_optional(model_cls: type[BaseModel]) -> type[BaseModel]:
    new_fields = {}

    for f_name, f_info in model_cls.model_fields.items():
        f_dct = f_info.asdict()
        new_fields[f_name] = (
            Annotated[f_dct['annotation'] | None, *f_dct['metadata'], Field(**f_dct['attributes'])],
            None,
        )

    return create_model(
        f'{model_cls.__name__}Optional',
        __base__=model_cls,  # (1)!
        **new_fields,
    )
```

### Validate using alias only with validate_by_alias=True

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/alias.md

Set validate_by_alias=True and validate_by_name=False to require the validation alias 'my_alias' for input. The attribute name 'my_field' is not accepted for validation.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


class Model(BaseModel):
    my_field: str = Field(validation_alias='my_alias')

    model_config = ConfigDict(validate_by_alias=True, validate_by_name=False)


print(repr(Model(my_alias='foo')))  # (1)!
#> Model(my_field='foo')
```

### Serialize using alias with serialize_by_alias=True

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/alias.md

Set serialize_by_alias=True in ConfigDict to use the serialization alias 'my_alias' when dumping the model. Serialization by alias is disabled by default.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


class Model(BaseModel):
    my_field: str = Field(serialization_alias='my_alias')

    model_config = ConfigDict(serialize_by_alias=True)


m = Model(my_field='foo')
print(m.model_dump())  # (1)!
#> {'my_alias': 'foo'}
```

### Validating union types with default smart mode

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/unions.md

Smart mode evaluates union members to find the best match based on exactness and valid fields set. Exact type matches for `int`, `str`, or `UUID` are preserved rather than coercing to the leftmost compatible type.

```python
from uuid import UUID

from pydantic import BaseModel


class User(BaseModel):
    id: int | str | UUID
    name: str


user_01 = User(id=123, name='John Doe')
print(user_01)
#> id=123 name='John Doe'
print(user_01.id)
#> 123
user_02 = User(id='1234', name='John Doe')
print(user_02)
#> id='1234' name='John Doe'
print(user_02.id)
#> 1234
user_03_uuid = UUID('cf57432e-809e-4353-adbd-9d5c0d733868')
user_03 = User(id=user_03_uuid, name='John Doe')
print(user_03)
#> id=UUID('cf57432e-809e-4353-adbd-9d5c0d733868') name='John Doe'
print(user_03.id)
#> cf57432e-809e-4353-adbd-9d5c0d733868
print(user_03_uuid.int)
#> 275603287559914445491632874575877060712
```

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

    my_field: str = Field(validation_alias='my_alias')

### Configure Pydantic models using class arguments

Passes configuration options directly as class arguments when defining a BaseModel subclass. Unlike model_config, class arguments such as frozen=True are recognized by static type checkers.

### Apply field_serializer to multiple fields

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/serialization.md

Use the @field_serializer decorator to apply the same serialization function to multiple fields. Pass '*' to apply to all fields, and set check_fields=False to skip field existence checks.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, field_serializer


class Model(BaseModel):
    f1: str
    f2: str

    @field_serializer('f1', 'f2', mode='plain')
    def capitalize(self, value: str) -> str:
        return value.capitalize()
```

### Configuring nested Pydantic models with model_config boundaries

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/config.md

Configuration does not propagate into nested Pydantic models and dataclasses because each model maintains its own configuration boundary. In this example, Parent's str_to_lower=True does not affect the nested User model.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class User(BaseModel):
    name: str


class Parent(BaseModel):
    user: User

    model_config = ConfigDict(str_to_lower=True)


print(Parent(user={'name': 'JOHN'}))
#> user=User(name='JOHN')
```

### model_dump(exclude_unset=...)

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/serialization.md

The `model_dump()` method serializes a model instance to a dictionary. The `exclude_unset` parameter excludes any field that was not explicitly set during instantiation (tracked via `model_fields_set`). Note that altering a field after instance creation will remove it from the unset fields.

```APIDOC
## model_dump(exclude_unset=...)

### Description
Serializes the model instance to a dictionary, excluding any field that was not explicitly set during instantiation. Pydantic tracks explicitly set fields via the `model_fields_set` property. Note that altering a field after instance creation will remove it from the unset fields.

### Method
`model_dump()`

### Parameters
- **exclude_unset** (bool) - Optional - If `True`, exclude fields that were not explicitly set during instantiation.

### Example
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class UserModel(BaseModel):
    name: str
    age: int = 18

user = UserModel(name='John')
print(user.model_fields_set)
#> {'name'}

print(user.model_dump(exclude_unset=True))
#> {'name': 'John'}
```
```

### Configure strict validation per field with Field(strict=...)

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/fields.md

Specify whether a field validates in strict or lax mode using Field(strict=...). In lax mode (strict=False), validatable types such as numeric strings are coerced into integers.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class User(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(strict=True)
    age: int = Field(strict=False)  # (1)!


user = User(name='John', age='42')  # (2)!
print(user)
#> name='John' age=42
```

### Raise bytes_too_short error when bytes are below min_length

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/errors/validation_errors.md

Use when the length of a bytes value is less than the field's min_length constraint. The example sets min_length=3 and passes b't'.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError


class Model(BaseModel):
    x: bytes = Field(min_length=3)


try:
    Model(x=b't')
except ValidationError as exc:
    print(repr(exc.errors()[0]['type']))
    #> 'bytes_too_short'
```

### Deprecate field using boolean flag in Field

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/fields.md

Set deprecated=True in Field to mark a field as deprecated without specifying a custom deprecation message. The generated JSON schema will reflect the deprecation status.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Model(BaseModel):
    deprecated_field: Annotated[int, Field(deprecated=True)]


print(Model.model_json_schema()['properties']['deprecated_field'])
#> {'deprecated': True, 'title': 'Deprecated Field', 'type': 'integer'}
```

### Raise string_not_ascii with StringConstraints ascii_only

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/errors/validation_errors.md

Setting ascii_only=True via StringConstraints raises string_not_ascii when the input string contains non-ASCII characters. The example validates 'café' against the constrained field.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import BaseModel, StringConstraints, ValidationError


class Model(BaseModel):
    v: Annotated[str, StringConstraints(ascii_only=True)]


try:
    Model(v='caf\u00e9')
except ValidationError as exc:
    print(repr(exc.errors()[0]['type']))
    #> 'string_not_ascii'
```

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class User(BaseModel):
    # Both fields aren't required:
    name: str = 'John Doe'
    age: int = Field(default=20)

### Field alias takes precedence over alias_generator

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/alias.md

When an explicit alias is set on a Field, it overrides the alias generated by alias_generator by default. The example shows validation using the explicit alias 'lang' and serialization with by_alias=True.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


def to_camel(string: str) -> str:
    return ''.join(word.capitalize() for word in string.split('_'))


class Voice(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(alias_generator=to_camel)

    name: str
    language_code: str = Field(alias='lang')


voice = Voice(Name='Filiz', lang='tr-TR')
print(voice.language_code)
#> tr-TR
print(voice.model_dump(by_alias=True))
#> {'Name': 'Filiz', 'lang': 'tr-TR'}
```

### Configure Pydantic dataclasses with ConfigDict

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/config.md

Passes a ConfigDict instance to the config argument of the Pydantic dataclass decorator. This example configures assignment validation and string length limits on dataclass fields.

```python
from pydantic import ConfigDict, ValidationError
from pydantic.dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(config=ConfigDict(str_max_length=10, validate_assignment=True))
class User:
    name: str


user = User(name='John Doe')
try:
    user.name = 'x' * 20
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)
    """
    1 validation error for User
    name
      String should have at most 10 characters [type=string_too_long, input_value='xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx', input_type=str]
    """
```

### Bound dict size with max_length to mitigate hash collisions

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/api/standard_library_types.md

Use the `max_length` constraint on a dict to limit the number of items when input is untrusted, since building a set or dictionary from crafted values can take quadratic time. Wrap the type with `Annotated` and `Field(max_length=100)` in a `TypeAdapter`.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import Field, TypeAdapter

ta = TypeAdapter(Annotated[dict[int, int], Field(max_length=100)])
```

### Define default values with Field keyword arguments for pyright

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/integrations/visual_studio_code.md

Passes `default` as an explicit keyword argument to `Field` so Pylance/pyright can correctly infer the field is optional. Using positional arguments works at runtime but causes static type checker errors due to dataclass transform limitations.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Knight(BaseModel):
    title: str = Field(default='Sir Lancelot')  # this is okay
    age: int = Field(
        23
    )  # this works fine at runtime but will case an error for pyright


lance = Knight()  # error: Argument missing for parameter "age"
```

### Raise no_such_attribute validation error with validate_assignment=True

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/errors/validation_errors.md

Raises a 'no_such_attribute' error when validate_assignment=True is set in the config and you assign a value to an attribute that is not an existing field. The example prints the error type from the caught ValidationError.

```python
from pydantic import ConfigDict, ValidationError, dataclasses


@dataclasses.dataclass(config=ConfigDict(validate_assignment=True))
class MyDataclass:
    x: int


m = MyDataclass(x=1)
try:
    m.y = 10
except ValidationError as exc:
    print(repr(exc.errors()[0]['type']))
    #> 'no_such_attribute'
```

### model_dump(include=...)

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/serialization.md

The `model_dump()` method serializes a model instance to a dictionary. The `include` parameter specifies which fields to include in the output, supporting sets, dictionaries, and nested field specifications. Using `False` to exclude a field in `include` is not supported.

```APIDOC
## model_dump(include=...)

### Description
Serializes the model instance to a dictionary, including only the specified fields. The `include` parameter accepts a set of field names or a dictionary mapping field names to `True` (include entirely) or nested inclusion specifications. Using `False` to exclude a field in `include` is not supported.

### Method
`model_dump()`

### Parameters
- **include** (set[str] | dict) - Optional - Fields to include. Can be a set of field names, or a dict where values are `True` (include the field) or nested dicts/sets for nested models and sequences.

### Example
```python
print(t.model_dump(include={'id': True, 'user': {'id'}}))
#> {'id': '1234567890', 'user': {'id': 42}}
```
```

### Generate aliases with a callable alias_generator

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/alias.md

Set ConfigDict.alias_generator to a callable to derive an alias for every field from its name. Here the lambda uppercases field names, so validation accepts uppercase keys and model_dump(by_alias=True) outputs uppercase keys.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Tree(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(
        alias_generator=lambda field_name: field_name.upper()
    )

    age: int
    height: float
    kind: str


t = Tree.model_validate({'AGE': 12, 'HEIGHT': 1.2, 'KIND': 'oak'})
print(t.model_dump(by_alias=True))
#> {'AGE': 12, 'HEIGHT': 1.2, 'KIND': 'oak'}
```

### Customizing core schema with __get_pydantic_core_schema__ and Annotated

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/internals/architecture.md

Applies custom metadata wrappers using __get_pydantic_core_schema__ to modify core schemas recursively via GetCoreSchemaHandler.

```python
from typing import Annotated, Any

from pydantic_core import CoreSchema

from pydantic import GetCoreSchemaHandler, TypeAdapter


class MyStrict:
    @classmethod
    def __get_pydantic_core_schema__(
        cls, source: Any, handler: GetCoreSchemaHandler
    ) -> CoreSchema:
        schema = handler(source)  # (1)!
        schema['strict'] = True
        return schema


class MyGt:
    @classmethod
    def __get_pydantic_core_schema__(
        cls, source: Any, handler: GetCoreSchemaHandler
    ) -> CoreSchema:
        schema = handler(source)  # (2)!
        schema['gt'] = 1
        return schema


ta = TypeAdapter(Annotated[int, MyStrict(), MyGt()])
```

### Using the Strict metadata class and strict type aliases

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/strict_mode.md

Apply strict mode with the annotated pattern using `Strict()` or dedicated strict type aliases like `StrictInt`. This serves as an alternative to `Field(strict=True)`.

```python
from typing import Annotated
from uuid import UUID

from pydantic import BaseModel, Strict, StrictInt

### Catching Frozen Model Mutation Errors with Pyrefly

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/integrations/pyrefly.md

Mutating fields on frozen models raises type errors in Pyrefly whether frozen is set via class kwargs or ConfigDict. Standard type checkers without Pydantic support miss the ConfigDict frozen check.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Model1(BaseModel, frozen=True):
    x: int


class Model2(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
    x: int


model1 = Model1(x=0)
model1.x = 1  # validation error: mutating a frozen field

model2 = Model2(x=0)
model2.x = 1  # validation error: mutating a frozen field
```

```output
ERROR Cannot set field `x` [read-only]
  --> foo.py:11:1
   |
11 | model1.x = 1  # validation error: mutating a frozen field
   | ^^^^^^^^
   |
  This field belongs to a frozen Pydantic model
ERROR Cannot set field `x` [read-only]
  --> foo.py:14:1
   |
14 | model2.x = 1  # validation error: mutating a frozen field
   | ^^^^^^^^
   |
  This field belongs to a frozen Pydantic model
```

### Ignore validation errors in last element with experimental_allow_partial

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/experimental.md

Demonstrates parsing incomplete JSON streams by setting experimental_allow_partial=True in validate_json. All validation errors occurring in the incomplete final element are ignored, returning valid instances for preceding complete items.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from annotated_types import MinLen

from pydantic import BaseModel, TypeAdapter


class MyModel(BaseModel):
    a: int
    b: Annotated[str, MinLen(5)]


ta = TypeAdapter(list[MyModel])
v = ta.validate_json(
    '[{"a": 1, "b": "12345"}, {"a": 1,',
    experimental_allow_partial=True,
)
print(v)
#> [MyModel(a=1, b='12345')]
```

### Use standard library dataclasses in BaseModel with instance revalidation

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/dataclasses.md

Use a stdlib dataclass as a field type in a BaseModel with ConfigDict(revalidate_instances='always') to enforce validation on model instantiation.

```python
import dataclasses

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, ValidationError


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class User:
    name: str


class Foo(BaseModel):
    # Required so that pydantic revalidates the model attributes:
    model_config = ConfigDict(revalidate_instances='always')

    user: User | None = None


# nothing is validated as expected:
user = User(name=['not', 'a', 'string'])
print(user)
#> User(name=['not', 'a', 'string'])


try:
    Foo(user=user)
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)
    """
    1 validation error for Foo
    user.name
      Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=['not', 'a', 'string'], input_type=list]
    """

foo = Foo(user=User(name='pika'))
try:
    foo.user.name = 'bulbi'
except dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError as e:
    print(e)
    #> cannot assign to field 'name'
```

### Raise bytes_invalid_encoding error for invalid hex bytes

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/errors/validation_errors.md

Use when a bytes value is invalid under the configured encoding. With val_json_bytes set to 'hex', the input 'a' is invalid hex because it has an odd number of digits.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError


class Model(BaseModel):
    x: bytes
    model_config = {'val_json_bytes': 'hex'}


try:
    Model(x='a')
except ValidationError as exc:
    print(repr(exc.errors()[0]['type']))
    #> 'bytes_invalid_encoding'
```

### model_dump(exclude=...)

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/serialization.md

The `model_dump()` method serializes a model instance to a dictionary. The `exclude` parameter specifies which fields to exclude from the output, supporting sets, dictionaries, and nested field specifications. Field-level exclusion (via `Field(exclude=True)`) takes priority over this parameter.

```APIDOC
## model_dump(exclude=...)

### Description
Serializes the model instance to a dictionary, excluding the specified fields. The `exclude` parameter accepts a set of field names or a dictionary mapping field names to `True` (exclude entirely) or nested exclusion specifications. Field-level exclusion (via `Field(exclude=True)`) takes priority over this parameter.

### Method
`model_dump()`

### Parameters
- **exclude** (set[str] | dict) - Optional - Fields to exclude. Can be a set of field names, or a dict where values are `True` (exclude the field) or nested dicts/sets for nested models and sequences.

### Example
```python
# using a set:
print(t.model_dump(exclude={'user', 'value'}))
#> {'id': '1234567890'}

# using a dictionary:
print(t.model_dump(exclude={'user': {'username', 'password'}, 'value': True}))
#> {'id': '1234567890', 'user': {'id': 42}}
```
```

### Restrict values with typing.Literal in a Pydantic model

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/api/standard_library_types.md

Use `Literal` to allow only specific literal values. Pydantic validates literals in strict mode, so `quantity='1'` fails even though `1` is allowed.

```python
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError


class Pie(BaseModel):
    flavor: Literal['apple', 'pumpkin']
    quantity: Literal[1, 2] = 1


Pie(flavor='apple')
Pie(flavor='pumpkin')
try:
    Pie(flavor='cherry')
except ValidationError as e:
    print(str(e))
    """
    1 validation error for Pie
    flavor
      Input should be 'apple' or 'pumpkin' [type=literal_error, input_value='cherry', input_type=str]
    """

try:
    Pie(flavor='apple', quantity='1')
except ValidationError as e:
    print(str(e))
    """
    1 validation error for Pie
    quantity
      Input should be 1 or 2 [type=literal_error, input_value='1', input_type=str]
    """
```

### Applying constraints to union types with None

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/fields.md

Constraints applied to a union containing None or MISSING automatically apply to the remaining types, using either Field or Annotated.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Model(BaseModel):
    positive: int | None = Field(gt=0)
    # Also works with the annotated pattern:
    negative: Annotated[int | None, Field(lt=0)]
```

### Attach metadata to top-level union types vs inner types

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/fields.md

Contrasts applying Field metadata to an inner type versus a top-level union type. Metadata like deprecated must be attached to the top-level union type to take effect on the field.

```python
class Model(BaseModel):
    field_bad: Annotated[int, Field(deprecated=True)] | None = None  # (1)!
    field_ok: Annotated[int | None, Field(deprecated=True)] = None  # (2)!

### Adding type constraints with Field

### Constrain a string field with StringConstraints to_lower

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/api/standard_library_types.md

Use StringConstraints metadata with Annotated to apply string constraints such as to_lower. The constrained field converts 'TEST' to 'test', while an unconstrained str field is accepted as-is.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import BaseModel, StringConstraints


class StringModel(BaseModel):
    str_value: str = ""
    constrained_str_value: Annotated[str, StringConstraints(to_lower=True)] = ""


print(StringModel(str_value="test").str_value)
#> test
print(StringModel(constrained_str_value='TEST').constrained_str_value)
#> test
```

### Demonstrate unexpected type coercion with left_to_right union ordering

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/unions.md

Shows how member ordering in `left_to_right` mode can lead to surprising results in lax mode. A numeric string like `'456'` matches the first member `int` via coercion instead of matching `str`.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class User(BaseModel):
    id: int | str = Field(union_mode='left_to_right')


print(User(id=123))  # (1)
#> id=123
print(User(id='456'))  # (2)
#> id=456
```

### Modify Core Schema In-Place with __get_pydantic_core_schema__

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/json_schema.md

Call the handler to obtain the default core schema, mutate it in place (e.g., adding constraints like max_length), and return the updated schema. You must return a schema even when mutating in place.

```python
from typing import Annotated, Any

from pydantic_core import ValidationError, core_schema

from pydantic import BaseModel, GetCoreSchemaHandler


class SmallString:
    def __get_pydantic_core_schema__(
        self,
        source: type[Any],
        handler: GetCoreSchemaHandler,
    ) -> core_schema.CoreSchema:
        schema = handler(source)
        assert schema['type'] == 'str'
        schema['max_length'] = 10  # modify in place
        return schema


class MyModel(BaseModel):
    value: Annotated[str, SmallString()]


try:
    MyModel(value='too long!!!!!')
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)
    """
    1 validation error for MyModel
    value
      String should have at most 10 characters [type=string_too_long, input_value='too long!!!!!', input_type=str]
    """
```

### Serialize Pydantic models in multiple ways

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/why.md

Serializes a model instance to standard Python dictionaries, JSON-compatible types, and a raw JSON string. Demonstrates customization using `exclude_unset`, `exclude`, `mode='json'`, and `exclude_defaults`.

```python
from datetime import datetime

from pydantic import BaseModel


class Meeting(BaseModel):
    when: datetime
    where: bytes
    why: str = 'No idea'


m = Meeting(when='2020-01-01T12:00', where='home')
print(m.model_dump(exclude_unset=True))
#> {'when': datetime.datetime(2020, 1, 1, 12, 0), 'where': b'home'}
print(m.model_dump(exclude={'where'}, mode='json'))
#> {'when': '2020-01-01T12:00:00', 'why': 'No idea'}
print(m.model_dump_json(exclude_defaults=True))
#> {"when":"2020-01-01T12:00:00","where":"home"}
```

### Validate and serialize datetime.time with Pydantic BaseModel

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/api/standard_library_types.md

Defines a model with a `time` field. In Python mode, `model_dump()` returns a `datetime.time` instance; in JSON mode, `model_dump_json()` returns an RFC 3339 string.

```python
from datetime import time

from pydantic import BaseModel


class Meeting(BaseModel):
    t: time


m = Meeting(t=time(4, 8, 16))

print(m.model_dump())
#> {'t': datetime.time(4, 8, 16)}
print(m.model_dump_json())
#> {"t":"04:08:16"}
```

### Access metadata in @field_validator with ValidationInfo

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/migration.md

Demonstrates accessing config and field metadata in Pydantic V2 using the info parameter of type ValidationInfo. In V2, info.config provides dictionary access and cls.model_fields[info.field_name] accesses field properties.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationInfo, field_validator


class Model(BaseModel):
    x: int

    @field_validator('x')
    def val_x(cls, v: int, info: ValidationInfo) -> int:
        assert info.config is not None
        print(info.config.get('title'))
        #> Model
        print(cls.model_fields[info.field_name].is_required())
        #> True
        return v


Model(x=1)
```

### Validate datetime timezone constraints using Annotated metadata

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/examples/custom_validators.md

Construct a custom validator attached to `typing.Annotated` using `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` and `no_info_wrap_validator_function`. The wrap validator runs standard Pydantic validation via `handler(value)` before asserting that the parsed datetime matches the specified timezone constraint or is timezone-naive. Raises `PydanticUserError` when given an invalid timezone name and `ValidationError` on timezone mismatch.

```python
import datetime as dt
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pprint import pprint
from typing import Annotated, Any

import pytz
from pydantic_core import CoreSchema, core_schema

from pydantic import (
    GetCoreSchemaHandler,
    PydanticUserError,
    TypeAdapter,
    ValidationError,
    ValidatorFunctionWrapHandler,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MyDatetimeValidator:
    tz_constraint: str | None = None

    def tz_constraint_validator(
        self,
        value: Any,
        handler: ValidatorFunctionWrapHandler,  # (1)!
    ):
        """Validate tz_constraint and tz_info."""
        result = handler(value)  # (2)!

        # handle naive datetimes
        if self.tz_constraint is None:
            assert (
                result.tzinfo is None
            ), 'tz_constraint is None, but provided value is tz-aware.'
            return result

        # validate tz_constraint and tz-aware tzinfo
        if self.tz_constraint not in pytz.all_timezones:
            raise PydanticUserError(
                f'Invalid tz_constraint: {self.tz_constraint}',
                code='unevaluable-type-annotation',
            )
        assert self.tz_constraint == str(
            result.tzinfo
        ), f'Invalid tzinfo: {str(result.tzinfo)}, expected: {self.tz_constraint}'

        return result

    def __get_pydantic_core_schema__(
        self,
        source_type: Any,
        handler: GetCoreSchemaHandler,
    ) -> CoreSchema:
        return core_schema.no_info_wrap_validator_function(
            self.tz_constraint_validator,
            handler(source_type),
        )


LA = 'America/Los_Angeles'
ta = TypeAdapter(Annotated[dt.datetime, MyDatetimeValidator(LA)])
print(
    ta.validate_python(dt.datetime(2023, 1, 1, 0, 0, tzinfo=pytz.timezone(LA)))
)
#> 2023-01-01 00:00:00-07:53

naive_ta = TypeAdapter(Annotated[dt.datetime, MyDatetimeValidator()])
print(naive_ta.validate_python('2023-01-01T00:00:00'))
#> 2023-01-01 00:00:00

LONDON = 'Europe/London'
try:
    ta.validate_python(
        dt.datetime(2023, 1, 1, 0, 0, tzinfo=pytz.timezone(LONDON))
    )
except ValidationError as ve:
    pprint(ve.errors(), width=100)
    """
    [{'ctx': {'error': AssertionError('Invalid tzinfo: Europe/London, expected: America/Los_Angeles')},
    'input': datetime.datetime(2023, 1, 1, 0, 0, tzinfo=<DstTzInfo 'Europe/London' LMT-1 day, 23:59:00 STD>),
    'loc': (),
    'msg': 'Assertion failed, Invalid tzinfo: Europe/London, expected: America/Los_Angeles',
    'type': 'assertion_error',
    'url': 'https://errors.pydantic.dev/2/v/assertion_error'}]
    """
```

### Structural pattern matching on a Pydantic model

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/models.md

Uses Python 3.10 match-case (PEP 636) to match a model's field value and bind the name. Note that match-case is syntactic sugar for attribute access and comparison, not model creation.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel


class Pet(BaseModel):
    name: str
    species: str


a = Pet(name='Bones', species='dog')

match a:
    # match `species` to 'dog', declare and initialize `dog_name`
    case Pet(species='dog', name=dog_name):
        print(f'{dog_name} is a dog')
#> Bones is a dog
    # default case
    case _:
        print('No dog matched')
```

### Customizing JSON Schema using __get_pydantic_json_schema__

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/errors/usage_errors.md

Defines custom JSON schema modifications in V2 using __get_pydantic_json_schema__ with CoreSchema and GetJsonSchemaHandler.

```python
from typing import Any

from pydantic_core import CoreSchema

from pydantic import BaseModel, GetJsonSchemaHandler


class Model(BaseModel):
    @classmethod
    def __get_pydantic_json_schema__(
        cls, core_schema: CoreSchema, handler: GetJsonSchemaHandler
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        json_schema = super().__get_pydantic_json_schema__(core_schema, handler)
        json_schema = handler.resolve_ref_schema(json_schema)
        json_schema.update(examples=['example'])
        return json_schema


print(Model.model_json_schema())
"""
{'examples': ['example'], 'properties': {}, 'title': 'Model', 'type': 'object'}
"""

```

### Customize $ref references using ref_template

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/json_schema.md

Specify a custom prefix format for `$ref` definitions using the `ref_template` parameter in `json_schema()` or `model_json_schema()`. Definitions remain stored under `$defs` while referencing the custom schema path format.

```python
import json

from pydantic import BaseModel
from pydantic.type_adapter import TypeAdapter


class Foo(BaseModel):
    a: int


class Model(BaseModel):
    a: Foo


adapter = TypeAdapter(Model)

print(
    json.dumps(
        adapter.json_schema(ref_template='#/components/schemas/{model}'),
        indent=2,
    )
)
"""
{
  "$defs": {
    "Foo": {
      "properties": {
        "a": {
          "title": "A",
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "a"
      ],
      "title": "Foo",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "properties": {
    "a": {
      "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Foo"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "a"
  ],
  "title": "Model",
  "type": "object"
}
"""
```

### Define custom datetime validator via Annotated metadata

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/examples/custom_validators.md

Implements a custom dataclass validator with bounds checking for timezone UTC offsets using `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` and `TypeAdapter`. Validates timezone-aware datetime instances and raises a `ValidationError` when the offset is out of bounds.

```python
import datetime as dt
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pprint import pprint
from typing import Annotated, Any

import pytz
from pydantic_core import CoreSchema, core_schema

from pydantic import (
    GetCoreSchemaHandler,
    TypeAdapter,
    ValidationError,
    ValidatorFunctionWrapHandler,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MyDatetimeValidator:
    lower_bound: int
    upper_bound: int

    def validate_tz_bounds(
        self, value: Any, handler: ValidatorFunctionWrapHandler
    ):
        """Validate and test bounds"""
        assert self.lower_bound <= self.upper_bound, 'Invalid bounds'

        result = handler(value)
        assert result.utcoffset() is not None, 'UTC offset must exist'

        hours_offset = result.utcoffset().total_seconds() / 3600
        assert (
            self.lower_bound <= hours_offset <= self.upper_bound
        ), 'Value out of bounds'

        return result

    def __get_pydantic_core_schema__(
        self,
        source_type: Any,
        handler: GetCoreSchemaHandler,
    ) -> CoreSchema:
        return core_schema.no_info_wrap_validator_function(
            self.validate_tz_bounds,
            handler(source_type),
        )


LA = 'America/Los_Angeles'  # UTC-7 or UTC-8
ta = TypeAdapter(Annotated[dt.datetime, MyDatetimeValidator(-10, -5)])
print(
    ta.validate_python(dt.datetime(2023, 1, 1, 0, 0, tzinfo=pytz.timezone(LA)))
)
#> 2023-01-01 00:00:00-07:53

print(ta.validate_json('"2023-01-01T00:00:00-08:00"'))
#> 2023-01-01 00:00:00-08:00

LONDON = 'Europe/London'
try:
    print(
        ta.validate_python(
            dt.datetime(2023, 1, 1, 0, 0, tzinfo=pytz.timezone(LONDON))
        )
    )
except ValidationError as e:
    pprint(e.errors(), width=100)
    """
    [{'ctx': {'error': AssertionError('Value out of bounds')},
    'input': datetime.datetime(2023, 1, 1, 0, 0, tzinfo=<DstTzInfo 'Europe/London' LMT-1 day, 23:59:00 STD>),
    'loc': (),
    'msg': 'Assertion failed, Value out of bounds',
    'type': 'assertion_error',
    'url': 'https://errors.pydantic.dev/2/v/assertion_error'}]
    """
```

### TypeAdapter validation methods

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/alias.md

The TypeAdapter class provides validation methods that accept the `by_alias` and `by_name` flags to control whether attribute names or aliases are used for population. By default, `by_alias` is True and `by_name` is False.

```APIDOC
## TypeAdapter validation methods

### Description
The TypeAdapter class provides validation methods that accept the `by_alias` and `by_name` flags to control whether attribute names or aliases are used for population. By default, `by_alias` is True and `by_name` is False.

### Method
`TypeAdapter.validate_python()`, `TypeAdapter.validate_json()`, `TypeAdapter.validate_strings()`

### Parameters
- **data** (any) - Required - The input data to validate.
- **by_alias** (bool) - Optional - Whether to use aliases for validation. Default: True.
- **by_name** (bool) - Optional - Whether to use attribute names for validation. Default: False.

### Request Example
```python
adapter = TypeAdapter(Model)
m = adapter.validate_python(
    {'my_alias': 'foo'},
    by_alias=True,
    by_name=False,
)
```

### Response
Returns a validated instance.

#### Response Example
```python
Model(my_field='foo')
```
```

### Customize Field JSON Schema Attributes

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/concepts/json_schema.md

Customizes field schema metadata such as description, title, examples, and additional properties via json_schema_extra using Field() and Annotated.

```python
import json
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import BaseModel, EmailStr, Field, SecretStr


class User(BaseModel):
    age: int = Field(description='Age of the user')
    email: Annotated[EmailStr, Field(examples=['marcelo@mail.com'])]  # (1)!
    name: str = Field(title='Username')
    password: SecretStr = Field(
        json_schema_extra={
            'title': 'Password',
            'description': 'Password of the user',
            'examples': ['123456'],
        }
    )


print(json.dumps(User.model_json_schema(), indent=2))
"""
{
  "properties": {
    "age": {
      "description": "Age of the user",
      "title": "Age",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "email": {
      "examples": [
        "marcelo@mail.com"
      ],
      "format": "email",
      "title": "Email",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "name": {
      "title": "Username",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "password": {
      "description": "Password of the user",
      "examples": [
        "123456"
      ],
      "format": "password",
      "title": "Password",
      "type": "string",
      "writeOnly": true
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "age",
    "email",
    "name",
    "password"
  ],
  "title": "User",
  "type": "object"
}
"""
```

### Include decimal pattern in JSON Schema by overriding get_decimal_pattern

Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/docs/api/standard_library_types.md

Since v2.14 the JSON Schema no longer includes a pattern for max_digits and decimal_places by default. Subclass GenerateJsonSchema and override get_decimal_pattern to restore it; the generated pattern accounts for exponents and allow_inf_nan and avoids lookahead assertions.

```python
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import Field, TypeAdapter
from pydantic.json_schema import GenerateJsonSchema


class MyGenerateJsonSchema(GenerateJsonSchema):
    def get_decimal_pattern(self, schema):
        return self.build_decimal_pattern(schema)


ta = TypeAdapter(Annotated[Decimal, Field(max_digits=5, decimal_places=2)])
print(
    ta.json_schema(schema_generator=MyGenerateJsonSchema, mode='serialization')
)
"""
{
    'pattern': '^-?(?:(?:0|[1-9][0-9]{0,2})(?:\\.[0-9]{1,2}0*)?|0E[+-][1-9][0-9]*|[1-9](?:\\.[0-9]+)?E\\+[1-2])$',
    'type': 'string',
}
"""
```
